title: PowerPoint on the web: reference an attached deck's style when creating a presentation with Copilot Agent Mode
summary: Hold: the default-state field overlooks the documented user choice to attach a reference deck and request slides in its style. The statement that no source describes a change to existing behaviour also conflicts with the release note's explicit before-and-after description. The licence-assignment path and PowerShell call are supported.

claims.quote: Searched: 'Agent Mode' in the complete 555879 release-note entry at learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/release-notes; read its description, What changed, Why, Try this and impact paragraphs. The entry calls it Copilot in PowerPoint.

claims.claim: The capability's default state is unknown.
claims.quote: Use the 'Attach file' feature to select an existing PowerPoint deck. Request Copilot to generate slides using the attached deck’s style.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to 'user-opt-in': the standard includes a capability that each user chooses to use. Replace the default-state uncertainty in Why it matters with 'The release note describes users choosing an attached reference deck and requesting slides in its style.' Keep any question about tenant-wide rollout availability separate from this usage default. The targeted admin-switch searches found no setting specific to this capability.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated an administrator action required on arrival for this specific capability.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot PowerPoint reference attached deck theme styles admin setting disable default license pricing 555879' and 'Copilot PowerPoint reference attached deck style administration turn off setting default'; opened release-notes, copilot-overview and copilot-controls-overview on Learn.

claims.claim: No source says existing behaviour changes.
claims.quote: Copilot in PowerPoint now supports attaching an existing presentation when creating and editing a new one. Previously, new presentations used default themes. Now, Copilot applies the attached file’s theme and styles to the new deck, ensuring design consistency.
claims.fix: Remove 'and no source says existing behaviour changes'. The release note explicitly describes changed presentation-creation behaviour; its user steps, rather than a claim that nothing changes, establish that using the attached style is a user choice.

claims.claim: The licence-assignment path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
